instruction: You have a persistent project memory available through the {server} MCP server. Search it with {tool} BEFORE answering any question about this repository's conventions, tooling, commands, or history, and before recommending a command you have not verified against it. It holds decisions and hazards that are not derivable from the code, and the notes below do not contain all of them.

notes.this_arm: recall_rerank is `recall` with one setting changed, run as its PAIR inside one grid rather than as a second run. Diff this file against adapters/recall/config.frozen.json and the difference is exactly three keys: extra_env, package_pin and remote_python_env. Same tenant, same generation, same embedder, same strict gate, same eight tools, same server_name and tool_prefix, and an instruction that scripts/pilot.py derives from the SAME function rather than from a copied file, so the two arms cannot drift apart in the one place a difference would be invisible.
notes.reranker: ON, `voyage:rerank-2.5`, which is what `recall` deliberately does not do. Named explicitly rather than as the bare alias `voyage`, because the alias resolves to whatever DEFAULT_VOYAGE_RERANK_MODEL points at and a record should name the model that ran. It costs a Voyage rerank API call per query on top of the query embedding. ⚠️ Two hazards, both real and both stated rather than designed around. (1) recall_mcp.factories._new_reranker builds FallbackReranker(primary=Voyage, fallback=CrossEncoderReranker(ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2)) EAGERLY, so the local cross-encoder is downloaded and loaded even when Voyage answers every call; there is no configuration in 0.11.0 that selects Voyage alone. (2) That eager build is what hung reproducibly on this host during preregistration 014's measurement, server idle at 0.3% CPU with every call timing out at 90s, HuggingFace reachable, no root cause found. FallbackReranker counts and logs every fallback, so a run cannot silently measure a blend of the two rerankers, and that counter is the thing to read before believing any number this arm produces.
notes.package_pin: The `rerank` extra is a declared extra of the SAME published 0.11.0 wheel, not a checkout, so preregistration 012's requirement that this arm run a published artefact still holds. Verified 2026-09-02 on the bench venv: without it, RECALL_RERANK=1 with a Voyage model raises `ImportError: CrossEncoderReranker requires: pip install "recall-rag[rerank]"` at construction, with a valid VOYAGE_API_KEY present. The failure is at server start, not a silently unreranked search.
notes.remote_python: A SEPARATE interpreter from `recall`'s, named by its own variable. The rerank extra pulls torch and transformers into the environment, and installing them into the venv `recall` runs would change the artifact every published run was measured on in order to serve an arm that never touches them. Two venvs cost disk; one shared venv would cost the ability to say that `recall` is unchanged.
notes.allowed_tools: Identical to `recall`'s, deliberately. This arm varies retrieval, not surface area: an allow-list that differed would confound the reranker with the tools.
notes.embedder: Identical to `recall`'s. voyage-4 is used for representativeness rather than because it measured better; see adapters/recall/config.frozen.json, whose note on this is the one that governs both arms.
notes.transport: host, as `recall`. The server runs where the corpus lives and where the harness runs. Not a retrieval setting and cannot change what recall returns.
notes.location: Every host-specific value is named here and supplied by the environment, never stored, because this file is published with each run and a host inventory is disclosure on its own. See adapters/recall/location.example.env.
